draft:
We would recognize the words born again at once, yet for us new birth was a public event in the church, celebrated in hymn, and not a private moment of conversion [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our churches sang of baptism as a womb [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our churches sang of the shining garments of the newly baptized, and of the sealing, the sign set on each one who came up from the water [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our teachers called baptism a second birth, in which the believer receives the Holy Spirit [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

We did not believe in anything like the rapture [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our picture of the end was older: death's kingdom, which has ruled since Adam, had already been broken into by one Man [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

At the end, the dead rise the way seed rises, and the Judge repays everyone what is due [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

The sage wrote a whole letter on death and the last times, and there is no rapture in it [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].

What he preached was resurrection [[syr.dw.born-again-endtimes]] [[as:paraphrase]].
